title: The alternating-series bracket, dual form: every partial sum sits at or below the odd bracket
statement: For a nonnegative, non-increasing sequence a (∀k, 0 <= a k; ∀k, a(k+1) <= a k), and every m and i: the even-count partial sum E(m+i) and the odd-count partial sum O(m+i) both lie at or BELOW O(m). This is the dual of CReal.alternatingBracket (which brackets from BELOW, at E(m)): same induction shape on i, using the odd bracket's own one-step decrease (private o_step_le, mirroring e_step_le's one-step increase) instead. Needed because this development has no converges_upper_bound_shift primitive: closing an upper bound L <= O(m) on the true limit routes through converges_lower_bound_shift applied to the NEGATED sequence, which needs this dual bracket's per-index upper bound, not alternatingBracket's lower one.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.alternatingBracketUpper : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> CReal)) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> CReal.le CReal.zero (x0 x1))) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : AxNat) -> CReal.le (x0 (AxNat.succ x2)) (x0 x2))) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : AxNat) -> And (CReal.le (CReal.sumRange (fun (x5 : AxNat) => CReal.mul (CReal.pow (CReal.neg CReal.one) x5) (x0 x5)) (AxNat.add (AxNat.add x3 x4) (AxNat.add x3 x4))) (CReal.sumRange (fun (x5 : AxNat) => CReal.mul (CReal.pow (CReal.neg CReal.one) x5) (x0 x5)) (AxNat.succ (AxNat.add x3 x3)))) (CReal.le (CReal.sumRange (fun (x5 : AxNat) => CReal.mul (CReal.pow (CReal.neg CReal.one) x5) (x0 x5)) (AxNat.succ (AxNat.add (AxNat.add x3 x4) (AxNat.add x3 x4)))) (CReal.sumRange (fun (x5 : AxNat) => CReal.mul (CReal.pow (CReal.neg CReal.one) x5) (x0 x5)) (AxNat.succ (AxNat.add x3 x3)))))))))
